title: Vijayanagara, Bahmani, Malwa, Mewar, Sufi & Bhakti Movement
subject: History

questions.q: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka, who belonged to which dynasty?
questions.why: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I were formerly in the service of the Kakatiyas. After being reconverted to Hinduism by Saint Vidyaranya, they founded the first dynasty of Vijayanagara, the Sangama dynasty (1336–1485), named after their father.

questions.q: Which Vijayanagara ruler wrote the famous Telugu work 'Amuktamalyada'?
questions.why: Krishna Deva Raya (1509–1529) of the Tuluva dynasty was a great scholar. His court was adorned by the 'Ashtadiggajas' (eight poets). He wrote Amuktamalyada in Telugu and Jambavati Kalyanam in Sanskrit, earning titles like 'Andhra Bhoja'.

questions.q: The Persian traveler Abdur Razzaq visited the court of which Vijayanagara king?
questions.why: Abdur Razzaq, an ambassador of the Timurid ruler Shah Rukh, visited in 1443 during Deva Raya II's reign. He described Vijayanagara as 'unparalleled in the world'.

questions.q: The Battle of Talikota (1565), which led to the decline of the Vijayanagara Empire, is also known as:
questions.why: Fought on January 23, 1565, between Vijayanagara and the Deccan Sultanates. Betrayal led to the defeat of Rama Raya.

questions.q: Under whose reign did Nicolo Conti visit Vijayanagara in 1420 AD?
questions.why: Nicolo Conti was the first European traveler to visit. He documented the city's military strength and customs.

questions.q: Who founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336?
questions.why: They were sons of Sangama and founded the Sangama Dynasty on the banks of the Tungabhadra river with the blessings of Saint Vidyaranya.

questions.q: Which Vijayanagara ruler assumed the title 'Gajabetekara' (The Elephant Hunter)?
questions.why: Deva Raya II was the greatest ruler of the Sangama dynasty. He reorganized the army, recruiting Muslims for archery and cavalry, and expanded the empire.

questions.q: The 'Amuktamalyada' written by Krishna Deva Raya is in which language?
questions.why: It is a masterpiece of Telugu literature describing the wedding of Lord Ranganatha and Andal. KDR also wrote 'Jambavati Kalyanam' in Sanskrit.

questions.q: Which traveler called the Vijayanagara currency 'Pagoda'?
questions.why: The gold coins of Vijayanagara were called 'Varaha' (boar emblem) by locals, but Europeans, especially the Portuguese, called them 'Pagodas'.

questions.q: The 'Battle of Talikota' (1565) was fought between Vijayanagara and:
questions.why: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, and Bidar united to defeat Rama Raya. Berar did not join. This battle destroyed the magnificent city of Hampi.

questions.q: Who was the Portuguese traveler who visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Krishna Deva Raya?
questions.why: Paes (1520-22) described Vijayanagara as 'as large as Rome' and gave a vivid account of the Mahanavami Dibba festival.

questions.q: The 'Hazara Rama Temple' at Hampi served as:
questions.why: Built by Deva Raya I, it was dedicated to Lord Rama and was used exclusively by the royal family. Its walls depict scenes from the Ramayana.

questions.q: In the Vijayanagara administration, the term 'Ayagar' referred to:
questions.why: The Ayagar system was a feature of village administration where a body of 12 functionaries (Ayagars) managed village affairs.

questions.q: Which dynasty ruled Vijayanagara at the time of the Battle of Talikota?
questions.why: Sadashiva Raya was the puppet ruler of the Tuluva dynasty, but the actual power lay with his minister Aliya Rama Raya.

questions.q: Who was the court poet of Krishna Deva Raya known as 'Andhra Kavita Pitamaha'?
questions.why: He was the foremost of the Ashtadiggajas (8 poets) and wrote 'Manucharitam'. He is considered the father of Telugu poetry.

questions.q: The 'Nayankara System' of Vijayanagara was modeled on:
questions.why: Military chiefs (Nayaks) were given territories (Amaram) to govern and maintain troops, similar to the Iqta system of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.q: Nicolo Conti, the Italian traveler, visited Vijayanagara in:
questions.why: He visited during the reign of Deva Raya I and gave the first detailed European account of the city.

questions.q: The 'Vittala Temple' famous for its musical pillars was built during the reign of:
questions.why: Construction began under Devaraya II but major additions were made by KDR and Achyuta Raya. It houses the famous Stone Chariot.

questions.q: Who founded the 'Saluva' dynasty?
questions.why: He usurped the throne from the weak Sangama rulers to save the empire from disintegration in 1485.

questions.q: The Persian ambassador Abdur Razzaq came from the court of:
questions.why: Sent by the ruler of Herat, he visited the court of Deva Raya II in 1443 and praised the city's wealth.

questions.q: Who founded the Bahmani Kingdom in 1347?
questions.why: Original name Hasan Gangu. He revolted against Muhammad bin Tughlaq and established the capital at Gulbarga.

questions.q: The 'Gol Gumbaz' at Bijapur is the mausoleum of:
questions.why: It has the second-largest dome in the world and is famous for its 'Whispering Gallery' where sound echoes 7-10 times.

questions.q: Mahmud Gawan was the famous Prime Minister of which kingdom?
questions.why: He served under Muhammad Shah III. He was a Persian merchant who became a brilliant administrator and built a Madrasa at Bidar.

questions.q: Who built the 'Charminar' in Hyderabad?
questions.why: Built in 1591 to commemorate the eradication of a plague. He also founded the city of Hyderabad.

questions.q: Which Bahmani ruler was known as 'Wali' (Saint) due to his association with Sufi Gesu Daraz?
questions.why: He shifted the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar. He was a devotee of the Sufi saint Gesu Daraz.

questions.q: The 'Kitab-i-Nauras', a book on music, was written by:
questions.why: Ruler of Bijapur, he was called 'Jagat Guru' for his secular outlook. The book contains songs in praise of Hindu deities.

questions.q: Which Sultanate was the first to split from the Bahmani Kingdom?
questions.why: Fatehullah Imad Shah declared independence in 1490, founding the Imad Shahi dynasty of Berar.

questions.q: The city of 'Mustafabad' (Dabhol) was a key port for which kingdom?
questions.why: Horse trade with Persia and Arabia was conducted through this port, vital for the Deccan cavalry.

questions.q: Who annexed Golconda into the Mughal Empire in 1687?
questions.why: After an 8-month siege, he defeated Abul Hasan Tana Shah, the last Qutb Shahi ruler.

questions.q: The 'Madrasa of Mahmud Gawan' is located in:
questions.why: A magnificent three-story building reflecting Persian architecture, it was a major center of Islamic learning.

questions.q: Which Bhakti Saint was a cobbler by profession?
questions.why: Ravidas (Raidas) was a disciple of Ramananda and emphasized that caste has no value in the eyes of God.

questions.q: The philosophy of 'Vishishtadvaita' (Qualified Monism) was propounded by:
questions.why: He argued that the soul is distinct from Brahman but dependent on it, qualifying the non-dualism.

questions.q: Who founded the 'Pushtimarg' sect?
questions.why: He propounded 'Shuddhadvaita' (Pure Non-dualism) and emphasized the grace (pushti) of Krishna.

questions.q: The verses of which Bhakti Saint are included in the 'Guru Granth Sahib'?
questions.why: Kabir's dohas, along with those of Namdev and Raidas, form a significant part of the Sikh holy scripture.

questions.q: Who was the Guru of Mirabai?
questions.why: Mirabai, the Rajput princess and devotee of Krishna, accepted the low-caste saint Raidas as her spiritual guru.

questions.q: Which Saint popularized the 'Kirtan' system in Bengal?
questions.why: He was a devotee of Krishna and popularized public singing and dancing (Sankirtan) as a mode of worship.

questions.q: The 'Varkari' sect is associated with which region?
questions.why: Devotees of Lord Vithoba of Pandharpur. Key saints include Tukaram, Namdev, and Eknath.

questions.q: Shankaracharya is associated with which philosophy?
questions.why: Born in Kerala (8th century), he taught that the individual soul (Atman) and the Ultimate Reality (Brahman) are one.

questions.q: Who wrote 'Ramcharitmanas'?
questions.why: Written in Avadhi dialect during the reign of Akbar. It made the story of Rama accessible to the masses.

questions.q: The Bhakti Saint 'Shankardeva' belonged to:
questions.why: He founded the 'Ekasarana Dharma' (devotion to one God, Krishna) and introduced the Sattriya dance form.

questions.q: Who was the first Bhakti saint to use Hindi for preaching?
questions.why: He brought the Bhakti movement from South to North India and opened it to all castes and genders.

questions.q: The 'Abhangas' are associated with which Saint?
questions.why: Tukaram was a 17th-century Marathi poet-saint whose devotional poems to Vithoba are called Abhangas.

questions.q: Who wrote 'Sursagar'?
questions.why: A blind poet and devotee of Krishna, believed to be a disciple of Vallabhacharya.

questions.q: The 'Dasabodha' was written by:
questions.why: He was the spiritual guru of Shivaji Maharaj. The book is a guide on spiritual and practical life.

questions.q: Which Alvars saint was a woman?
questions.why: Andal is the only female Alvar among the 12 Vishnu devotees. Her hymns like 'Tiruppavai' are famous.

questions.q: Who was the founder of the Chishti order in India?
questions.why: He settled in Ajmer (Ajmer Sharif) in the late 12th century. His dargah is a major pilgrimage site.

questions.q: Which Sufi saint was called 'Mehboob-i-Ilahi' (Beloved of God)?
questions.why: He lived in Delhi and witnessed the reign of seven Sultans but never visited any court.

questions.q: The 'Suhrawardi' order was most popular in:
questions.why: Founded by Bahauddin Zakariya. Unlike Chishtis, they accepted royal patronage and lived comfortably.

questions.q: Who was the disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya known as 'Chiragh-i-Dehlvi'?
questions.why: He was the last great Sufi of the Chishti order in Delhi before it spread regionally.

questions.q: Which Sufi order adopted 'Pranayama' (Breath Control)?
questions.why: Yogic exercises were adopted by Chishti saints (like Nizamuddin Auliya), leading them to be called 'Siddhas'.

questions.q: Prince Dara Shikoh belonged to which Sufi order?
questions.why: He was influenced by Mullah Shah Badakhshi of the Qadiri order.

questions.q: The term 'Khanqah' refers to:
questions.why: A place where Sufi saints lived, prayed, and held gatherings (Sama).

questions.q: Who was the Sufi saint whose dargah is at Fatehpur Sikri?
questions.why: Akbar built his capital there to honor the saint who predicted the birth of his son Jahangir (Salim).

questions.q: The 'Naqshbandi' order was introduced in India by:
questions.why: It was the most orthodox order. Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi later revitalized it.

questions.q: Which Sufi saint is associated with the 'Qutub Minar'?
questions.why: Iltutmish dedicated the Qutub Minar to this saint, not to the Sultan Qutbuddin Aibak.

questions.q: Who built the 'Vijay Stambha' (Tower of Victory) at Chittor?
questions.why: Built to commemorate his victory over the combined armies of Malwa and Gujarat (1448).

questions.q: The 'Jahaz Mahal' is located in:
questions.why: Located in the Mandu fort (Malwa), it looks like a ship floating on water. Built by Ghiyas-ud-din Khilji.

questions.q: Who was the ruler of Mewar who fought the 'Battle of Khatoli' (1517)?
questions.why: He defeated Ibrahim Lodi in this battle, weakening the Lodi dynasty before Babur's arrival.

questions.q: Rani Roopmati and Baz Bahadur are associated with which region?
questions.why: Baz Bahadur was the last Sultan of Malwa. Their love story is legendary. Malwa was annexed by Akbar in 1561.

questions.q: Who founded the independent Sultanate of Gujarat?
questions.why: He was a governor under the Tughlaqs who declared independence and took the title Muzaffar Shah.

questions.q: Which ruler of Kashmir is called the 'Akbar of Kashmir'?
questions.why: He ruled from 1420-70, practiced religious tolerance, abolished Jizya, and patronized arts/literature.

questions.q: The 'Atala Masjid' is located in:
questions.why: Built by the Sharqi rulers (Ibrahim Shah Sharqi). It is a classic example of Jaunpur style architecture.

questions.q: Mahmud Begarha was a famous Sultan of:
questions.why: He ruled for 53 years. 'Begarha' refers to his conquest of two forts (Junagadh and Champaner).

questions.q: Who wrote 'Rajatarangini'?
questions.why: Written in the 12th century, it is a historical chronicle of the kings of Kashmir.

questions.q: The 'Sun Temple' of Konark was built by:
questions.why: Built in the 13th century by the Eastern Ganga dynasty ruler.

questions.q: Who were the primary founders of the Vijayanagara Empire?
questions.why: Brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I founded the empire in 1336 on the banks of the Tungabhadra river.

questions.q: The ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire are found at which modern-day site?
questions.why: Hampi (Karnataka) was the capital and is now a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its stunning ruins.

questions.q: Which river served as the lifeline of the Vijayanagara Empire?
questions.why: The city was strategically located on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra river.

questions.q: Who was the most famous ruler of the Tuluva dynasty of Vijayanagara?
questions.why: He ruled from 1509-1529 and is considered the greatest Vijayanagara king, known for military and cultural heights.

questions.q: What was the local name for the gold coins issued by Vijayanagara rulers?
questions.why: The coins were called 'Varaha' because they often featured the emblem of a boar (incarnation of Vishnu).

questions.q: The first dynasty to rule over Vijayanagara was the:
questions.why: Named after Sangama, the father of the founders Harihara and Bukka.

questions.q: The famous Vittala Temple with musical pillars is located in:
questions.why: It is one of the most iconic structures in Hampi, famous for its stone chariot and 56 musical pillars.

questions.q: Which Vijayanagara king assumed the title 'Andhra Bhoja'?
questions.why: He earned this title due to his immense patronage of Telugu literature and his own scholarly works.

questions.q: The Battle of Talikota (1565) resulted in the downfall of which empire?
questions.why: The empire was decisively defeated by the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates.

questions.q: How many dynasties in total ruled the Vijayanagara Empire?
questions.why: The dynasties were Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu.

questions.q: Who was the founder of the Bahmani Kingdom in 1347?
questions.why: Also known as Hasan Gangu, he revolted against the Delhi Sultanate to found the kingdom.

questions.q: What was the first capital of the Bahmani Kingdom?
questions.why: Gulbarga (Ahsanabad) served as the capital until it was shifted to Bidar by Ahmad Shah Wali.

questions.q: The Bahmani Kingdom eventually split into how many independent Sultanates?
questions.why: The 'Deccan Sultanates' were Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmednagar, Bidar, and Berar.

questions.q: In which city is the famous 'Gol Gumbaz' located?
questions.why: It is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah and features one of the largest domes in the world.

questions.q: The 'Charminar' of Hyderabad was built by which ruler?
questions.why: He built it in 1591 to mark the end of a plague and as the centerpiece of his new city, Hyderabad.

questions.q: Mahmud Gawan, the famous Prime Minister, served which kingdom?
questions.why: He was a brilliant administrator who strengthened the Bahmani state before being executed due to court intrigue.

questions.q: Golkonda was famous throughout the medieval world for which trade?
questions.why: The Golconda mines produced world-famous diamonds like the Koh-i-Noor.

questions.q: Which Sultanate was known for the Imad Shahi dynasty?
questions.why: Berar was the first to break away from the Bahmani Kingdom under the Imad Shahi line.

questions.q: The 'Whispering Gallery' is a famous feature of which monument?
questions.why: The dome's acoustics allow even a faint whisper to be heard on the opposite side.

questions.q: Who shifted the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar?
questions.why: He shifted the capital in 1424 to a more central and defensible location.

questions.q: Who built the 'Vijay Stambha' (Tower of Victory) at Chittor?
questions.why: Built in 1448 to celebrate his victory over the combined forces of Malwa and Gujarat.

questions.q: The kingdom of Mewar is located in which modern Indian state?
questions.why: Mewar, with its capital at Chittor (and later Udaipur), was a powerful Rajput stronghold.

questions.q: Baz Bahadur was the last independent ruler of which kingdom?
questions.why: He was a famous lover of music and arts; his kingdom was annexed by Akbar.

questions.q: The 'Jahaz Mahal' (Ship Palace) is located in which city?
questions.why: Mandu (Malwa) is famous for its Afghan-style architecture, including the Jahaz Mahal.

questions.q: Who was the ruler of Mewar at the time of the Battle of Khanwa against Babur?
questions.why: He led the Rajput confederacy against Babur in 1527.

questions.q: The 'Akbar of Kashmir' title is given to which ruler?
questions.why: He was known for his religious tolerance and welfare policies, much like the Mughal Emperor Akbar.

questions.q: Which city was the capital of the Sharqi dynasty, known as the 'Shiraz of the East'?
questions.why: Jaunpur became a great center of learning and culture under the Sharqi Sultans.

questions.q: Mahmud Begarha was the most powerful Sultan of which region?
questions.why: He ruled for over 50 years and conquered the forts of Junagadh and Champaner.

questions.q: The 'Atala Masjid' is a prime example of architecture in:
questions.why: Built by Ibrahim Shah Sharqi, it features a unique style without minarets.

questions.q: Chittor was the capital of which Rajput clan?
questions.why: The Sisodia Rajputs of Mewar held Chittor as their prestigious capital.

questions.q: Who was the founder of the Sikh religion?
questions.why: He founded the faith in the late 15th century, emphasizing one God and equality.

questions.q: Which Bhakti saint was a famous weaver from Varanasi?
questions.why: Kabir Das was a 15th-century poet-saint known for his 'Dohas' and criticism of ritualism.

questions.q: Guru Nanak was born at which place (now in Pakistan)?
questions.why: He was born in 1469 in the village of Talwandi.

questions.q: The Bhakti saint Ravidas (Raidas) was the spiritual guru of:
questions.why: Mirabai, the Rajput princess, became a disciple of the low-caste saint Ravidas.

questions.q: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu popularized the Bhakti movement in which region?
questions.why: He was a devotee of Krishna and popularized the 'Kirtan' form of worship.

questions.q: Who wrote the 'Ramcharitmanas'?
questions.why: Written in the Avadhi dialect during Akbar's time, making the Ramayana popular in North India.

questions.q: The only female saint among the 12 Alvars was:
questions.why: Andal was a famous Tamil poet-saint dedicated to Lord Vishnu.

questions.q: Who is the philosopher associated with 'Advaita' (Non-dualism)?
questions.why: He taught that the soul and Brahman are one and the same.

questions.q: Ramanujacharya propounded which philosophy in the 12th century?
questions.why: It is known as 'Qualified Monism', focusing on devotion to Vishnu.

questions.q: Namdev, a prominent Bhakti saint, belonged to which state?
questions.why: He was a tailor by profession and a key figure in the Varkari tradition.

questions.q: Who founded the Chishti order of Sufism in India?
questions.why: He settled in Ajmer and is the most revered Sufi saint in India.

questions.q: In which city is the 'Ajmer Sharif' Dargah located?
questions.why: It is the tomb of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti.

questions.q: Which Sufi saint was famously known as 'Mehboob-i-Ilahi'?
questions.why: Based in Delhi, he was one of the most influential Sufis of the Chishti order.

questions.q: In Sufism, what does the term 'Pir' represent?
questions.why: The Pir (or Murshid) guides the Murid (disciple) on the spiritual path.

questions.q: The term 'Murid' in Sufism refers to a:
questions.why: A Murid is a seeker or student who follows a Sufi master.

questions.q: The famous poet Amir Khusrau was a disciple of which Sufi saint?
questions.why: Khusrau was deeply devoted to Auliya and died shortly after the saint's death.

questions.q: The Dargah of Salim Chishti is located in which imperial city?
questions.why: Akbar built it in his capital to honor the saint who blessed him with a son.

questions.q: Baba Farid, whose verses are in the Guru Granth Sahib, belonged to which region?
questions.why: His Punjabi poetry influenced both Sufi and Sikh traditions.

questions.q: Which Sufi order was the most orthodox and strict in its practices?
questions.why: The Naqshbandi order, led by figures like Ahmad Sirhindi, was very conservative.

questions.q: What is a 'Khanqah' in the context of the Sufi movement?
questions.why: It was a community center where Sufi saints lived and taught their followers.
